page_information.description: The page's printed number and its classification.

page_number_integer.description: The printed page number from the transcription's <page_number> tag as an integer, with Roman numerals converted to their Arabic value; for a two-page spread, the left page's number. Null when the transcription has no <page_number> tag: numbers of footnotes, sections, figures and tables are not page numbers.

is_two_page_spread.description: True when the transcription covers two facing pages, shown by two consecutive <page_number> tags or by text that clearly belongs to two pages; false for a single page.

page_number_integer_end.description: For a two-page spread, the right page's number from its <page_number> tag, converted like page_number_integer; null for a single page or when the right page has no tag.

page_number_type.description: The numbering system of page_number_integer as printed: 'roman' or 'arabic'; 'none' when page_number_integer is null.

page_types.description: One to three classifications, all that apply to the page: 'content' for main body prose, 'abstract', 'preface' for forewords and dedications, 'appendix' for supplementary material, 'figures_tables_sources' for lists of figures or tables, 'table_of_contents', 'bibliography' for reference lists, 'title_page' for title and cover pages, 'index', 'blank', 'copyright' for imprint pages, and 'other' when none of these fits.

bullet_points.description: Bullet points that condense the page rather than restate it: 2-6 per page, scaled to its information density, each 10-25 words. Keep the page's main claims, findings with their numbers, datasets, methods, argument steps and named works; leave out restatements, illustrative examples, background and transitions. Together the bullets stay at most about a quarter of the length of the page's own text, so that a reader can scan a whole document quickly. A page that is mostly tables or figures gets one or two bullets naming what it contains and its key result. Every statement must come from the page; never add facts, figures or interpretations it does not give. Write formulas in LaTeX, $...$ inline and $$...$$ for display equations. Give bullets whenever page_types includes content, abstract, preface, appendix or figures_tables_sources; use null only for pages without summarizable prose, whose types are table_of_contents, bibliography, title_page, index, blank, copyright or other.

references.description: Every bibliographic citation on the page, from pages of any type, in APA style; null when the page cites nothing.

citation.description: The citation in APA style, built only from the bibliographic data the page states. Never invent, complete or paraphrase a title, venue or other detail; leave out what the page does not give rather than filling it with a placeholder.

is_partial.description: True when the page gives only an in-text pointer, such as author and year, op. cit. or ibid., without title and venue; false for a complete reference, such as a bibliography entry or a full footnote.
